item.title: Senco Gold to acquire 68% stake in August Jewellery for ₹68 crore
item.description: Senco Gold Ltd on Sunday said it has signed agreements to acquire a 68 per cent stake in August Jewellery Pvt Ltd, which operates the 'Melorra' brand, for Rs 68 crore. The investment will be made in multiple tranches, with completion targeted by February 2027, subject to fulfilment of specified conditions, the company said in a regulatory filing. It said that including the acquisition by a promoter group entity, the overall stake in August Jewellery will reach 79 per cent, following which the company will become a subsidiary of Senco Gold. The investment will happen through fresh equity issuance, with the funds intended for the company's growth and expansion, and the discharge of existing liabilities, the filing said. Senco Gold said the acquisition aligns with its digital and omnichannel strategy, particularly to cater to the fast-growing young consumer segment. item.title: JK Cement Q2FY27 result: Profit rises 6.3% to ₹169 cr; revenue jumps 23.7%
item.description: JK Cement Ltd on Saturday reported a 6.31 per cent increase in its consolidated net profit to Rs 169.3 crore for the September quarter of FY2026-27, helped by volume gains. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 159.25 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from JK Cement Ltd (JKCL), the flagship company of JK Organisation Group. Its revenue from operations was up 23.65 per cent to Rs 3,733.42 crore in the September quarter of FY27 compared to Rs 3,019.20 crore in the year-ago period. The company reported "robust volume growth and higher profitability despite cost pressures," JKCL said in its Investor Presentation. Its grey cement sales volume rose 21 per cent to 5.37 million tonnes (MT) in the second quarter of FY27. Similarly, white cement volume was up 13 per cent to 0.49 MT. item.title: AU Small Finance Bank Q2FY27 result: Net profit jumps 53% to ₹858 crore
item.description: AU Small Finance Bank on Saturday reported a 53 per cent surge in net profit at Rs 858 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 on the back of improvement in interest income. The lender had earned a net profit of Rs 561 crore in the year-ago period. Total income rose to Rs 6,382 crore in the quarter under review from Rs 5,224 crore in the same period a year ago, AU Small Finance Bank said in a regulatory filing. Interest income increased to Rs 5,612 crore as against Rs 4,511 crore in the corresponding second quarter of the previous year. Net interest income of the bank improved to Rs 2,820 crore in the July-September quarter, from Rs 2,144 crore in the September quarter of 2025, registering a growth of 32 per cent. Net interest margin increased to 5.8 per cent from 5.5 per cent at the end of September 2025. Asset quality of the bank also improved with gross non-performing assets (NPAs) rising to 1.99 per cent of gross advances at the end of the September quarter 2026

BPCL's standalone net profit declined to Rs 4,993 crore in July-September, the second quarter of fiscal 2027, from Rs 6,443 crore a year earlier, according to a company statement. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 1.58 lakh crore from Rs 1.22 lakh crore, while Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) fell nearly 14 per cent to Rs 9,437 crore from Rs 10,968 crore. India's second largest fuel retailer earned USD 32.53 on turning every barrel of crude oil into fuels like petrol and diesel in July-September, as compared to USD 10.78 a barrel gross refining margin in the same period a year back. "Right now the margin uptake that we are seeing is in the existing fixed price projects where AI is getting infused," Coforge Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Sudhir Singh, said during the company's earnings call. Coforge signed 8 large deals the highest number signed in a single quarter across North America, Europe and Australia, which led to a total contract value of the new orders of USD 1.04 billion during the reported quarter. The company increased the operational profit margin guidance to 17 per cent for the next year from the range of 15.5 per cent to 16 per cent.
